Register a plot panel declaratively (no Shiny boilerplate)

Source: R/panel-builder.R
register_plot_panel.Rd

A higher-level companion to register_panel(): describe the controls and a single plot function, and scroll generates the whole module — UI, control population, error surfacing, a Compute gate, downloads, spinner, and app-bar subset/view awareness. The silent-failure footguns of a hand-written server (a stray req(), an uncaught error) are handled for you.

Usage

register_plot_panel(
  id,
  plot,
  controls = list(),
  label = id,
  title = label,
  desc = NULL,
  after = NULL,
  before = NULL,
  compute = TRUE,
  csv = FALSE,
  style_caps = NULL
)

Arguments

id

Panel id (a single name).

plot

function(cells, input, data) returning a ggplot. cells is the active (subset/view-filtered) cell table; input exposes each control by its id; data is the handle (data$query1, data$con, data$manifest, …).

controls

A list of scroll_input_*() specs (see scroll_input). Wrap a look-only control in scroll_style_input() to place it in the plot's Style sheet instead of the control column.

label, title, desc, after, before

As in register_panel().

compute

If TRUE (default), the plot recomputes on a Compute button; FALSE makes it live (recompute on any control change).

csv

If TRUE, add a CSV button that exports the plot's source data. The plot function opts in by attaching the table to its result, e.g. attr(p, "scroll_source") <- df; p. Default FALSE.

style_caps

Scales & axes options for the plot's Style sheet, as in register_panel().

Value

Invisibly, id.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
register_plot_panel("counts",
  controls = list(scroll_input_column("grp", "Group", "categorical")),
  plot = function(cells, input, data) {
    ggplot2::ggplot(cells, ggplot2::aes(.data[[input$grp]])) + ggplot2::geom_bar()
  },
  label = "Counts", compute = FALSE)
} # }
